edition.en: Text as given on Chinese Wikisource.

basis.en: Song dynasty poem; the author died in 1210.

note.en: Written in 1186, when Lu You, past sixty, was in the capital waiting to take up a provincial post. The second couplet, a night of listening to rain and then flower-sellers in the morning lanes, is one of the loveliest in Song poetry. The rest is a mild complaint about idleness, practising calligraphy and whisking tea, and a resolve to be home by the spring festival of Qingming.
note.zh: 1186 年作，六十出头的陆游在临安等候赴任外州。“小楼一夜听春雨，深巷明朝卖杏花”是宋诗里最美的一联之一。其余是对闲散的温和抱怨：写写草书，玩玩分茶，打算在清明之前回到家里。

excerpt.orig: 小樓一夜聽春雨，深巷明朝賣杏花。
excerpt.en: All night in the little upstairs room I listened to the spring rain; / tomorrow morning, down the deep lanes, they will be selling apricot blossom.
excerpt.zh: 小楼一夜听春雨，深巷明朝卖杏花。

gloss.en: The taste of the world: the appeal of public life.
gloss.zh: 世味：人情世味，指做官的兴味。

gloss.en: The capital, here Lin’an (Hangzhou), the Southern Song capital.
gloss.zh: 京华：京城，指南宋都城临安（今杭州）。

gloss.en: 草 is cursive script. Lu You was a fine calligrapher; here he writes it to pass the time.
gloss.zh: 草：草书。闲作草，随意写草书消遣。

gloss.en: 分茶 was a Song tea game: hot water poured onto whisked powdered tea so that the fine froth (細乳) forms patterns and pictures.
gloss.zh: 分茶：宋代的一种点茶技艺，用沸水冲点茶末，使茶汤表面的细沫（细乳）幻化出图案。

gloss.en: Echoes Lu Ji: in the wind and dust of the capital a white robe turns black. Lu You tells his robe not to sigh.
gloss.zh: 化用陆机《为顾彦先赠妇》“京洛多风尘，素衣化为缁”。

gloss.en: Qingming, the spring festival for tending family graves, early in April.
gloss.zh: 清明：清明节，在公历四月初，有扫墓的习俗。
